frontend/apps/ppt-web/src/features/faults/components/FaultTimeline.tsx:142 renders a star rating via `'⭐'.repeat(Number.parseInt(entry.newValue, 10))` with no bounds check on entry.newValue (a server-supplied string on the 'rated' timeline entry). String.prototype.repeat throws RangeError for any negative count, so a malformed/out-of-range rating value (e.g. '-1') crashes the render of the whole FaultTimeline (and the enclosing FaultDetailPage) with an uncaught RangeError rather than degrading gracefully.

Non-integer or NaN inputs are harmless (repeat floors / treats NaN as 0), so the crash is specifically the negative-count path; a value above ~2^28 would instead throw on string length. Reachability requires the backend (or a tampered response) to emit a rated entry with an out-of-range newValue, hence confidence MEDIUM / severity MEDIUM (not runtime-reproduced).
Fix: clamp before repeat, e.g. `'⭐'.repeat(Math.max(0, Math.min(5, Number.parseInt(entry.newValue, 10) || 0)))`, or render N discrete star nodes from a clamped count.
